avis.texte: I suffer from adult hormonal acne. I got off the pill and my skin starting acting up again. I thought I'd give this a shot because my skin had a weird reaction from something and I had tiny bumps everywhere. I think it was from the facial wash or facial lotion my gym has. I tend to have sensitive skin. Anyway here's what I do - I wash my face, pat dry with a clean paper towel, spray the Daily Rescue Facial Spray, let it dry, and do the rest of my skincare. I am not kidding when I say I haven't had any breakouts! I use it any time I wash my face and my skin is so clear. No irritation, no breakouts, no dryness. This spray isn't just for people with eczema or rosacea - please try this if you have acne!

I assumed this product was only popular because of social media hype, but after trying a sample from Sephora, I was very pleased. I went through the bottle and bought more on Amazon. I found that it really helps prevent acne. I tend to pick at my face sometimes, and spraying this on after really helps to calm things down. I also found it to be really helpful for redness and irritation. I carry it with me to spritz on after working out to prevent sweat-induced acne. Most products geared toward acne strip the skin barrier, so it's great that this actually heals it while killing acne-causing bacteria. I wish it was a little less pricey, but hey, it works, so it's worth it.

Tower 28 is kind of the OG when it comes to hypochlorous acid sprays. While other companies were making HOCL before this, Tower 28 is really the brand that popularized it and turned it into such a mainstream, trendy skincare ingredient. This set includes two bottles, a 1 oz travel size and a 4 oz full size, which I genuinely love. I keep the smaller one in my gym bag and the larger one on my dressing table. My favorite way to use HOCL spray is at the gym. I mist my face before and after my workout, and since I started doing that, I no longer deal with itchy, irritated skin when I get sweaty. The formula works exactly as intended. It’s very calming and soothing on irritated skin. The smell is unmistakable. It smells almost exactly like a swimming pool right after a chlorine tablet has been added, but that’s actually how you know it’s legit. HOCL has that clean, chlorinated scent, and it dissipates quickly once it dries. HOCL is also a serious multitasker. It’s antimicrobial and does a great job neutralizing bacteria, fungi, and even viruses, all while still being gentle enough for regular skin use. I find it especially helpful for acne-prone moments, post-workout skin, or anytime my face feels reactive. That said, the price is high. HOCL does need to be carefully formulated and stabilized, but in my experience, as long as you’re buying from a reputable brand, one HOCL spray performs very similarly to another. avis.titre: **I REALLY hope people see this before deciding**
avis.texte: I’m going to be the odd one out rating this 1 star, and here’s why: •The price is ridiculous. Seriously, you are getting ripped off paying for this! I bought 2 GALLONS (256 oz) for CHEAPER than these measly 4 & 1oz bottles. •Speaking of that, there is nothing special or different about these other than the brand name. In fact, I think Tower 28’s formulation is inferior to others because it has sodium chloride in it AND they don’t even list the % of HOCl to water to salt! It’s my understanding, and I did extra research before reviewing this, that you do not want to add anything besides water to hypochlorous acid because it makes it LESS STABLE. You can probably find a 1 gallon for a decent price in the “you might also like” if you just scroll down a little. *Even if something is labeled as a household cleaner, if you check the ingredients and all it has is hypochlorous acid and water, it’s the SAME EXACT THING as the ones advertised as facial spray!* So yes, this works to disinfect skin (and surfaces) and helps with skincare concerns. But it’s also a ripoff in tiny bottles. With an extra ingredient that none of my HOCl sprays have ever had.
